newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-HUIZENGA PUTTING MARLINS UP FOR SALE.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-HUIZENGA PUTTING MARLINS UP FOR SALE.

text.p: Huizenga Holdings Chairman Wayne Huizenga said Thursday that he was putting the Florida Marlins baseball team on the sales block.
Huizenga said in a news release issued before a press conference that he had hired a Fort Lauderdale law firm to approach potential buyers and evaluate offers for the National League franchise.
Huizenga said he would seek a buyer who would keep the team in Florida.
"It's important for our fans and our season ticket holders. It's important for our loyals sponsors and friends. It's important for all South Florida," Huizenga said in a statement.
Huizenga said he hoped to sell the team, which he has said would lose $30 million in 1997, its fifth season, before the start of the 1998 baseball season next spring.
The Marlins went on a spending spree this past offseason to bring in manager Jim Leyland, third baseman Bobby Bonilla, pitcher Alex Fernandez and outfielder Moises Alou, among others.
Florida also gave their slugging right fielder Gary Sheffield a six-year deal worth more than $10 million per season.
Published reports have valued the Marlins at about $123 million. The Marlins, with a 45-30 record, are currently in second place in the National East, behind the Atlanta Braves.
